history: Italian piano looks like one word but carries several meanings, and all of them grow from Latin planus, ‘flat, level’. A flat surface gave the floor of a building: il primo piano is the first level above the ground. A drawing made on a flat sheet became a plan, un piano di lavoro. A flat, even movement became ‘slowly, gently’, so piano piano means ‘little by little’. In music piano means ‘soft’. Around 1700 the instrument maker Bartolomeo Cristofori built a keyboard that could play both soft and loud, and it was called gravicembalo col piano e forte. People shortened this to pianoforte and then to piano, and the instrument carries the word round the world.
historyEinfach: Piano comes from Latin planus, ‘flat’. A flat place is a floor, so piano means ‘floor of a building’. A plan is drawn on a flat page, so piano also means ‘plan’. A flat, calm way of moving is slow, so piano means ‘slowly’ and ‘softly’. The musical instrument has this name because it can play soft and loud sounds.

elsewhere.text: English took the instrument name from Italian in the 1800s. English plain and plane (the flat surface) come from the same Latin planus through French.
